_note: SYNTHETIC DATA. Minimal precedent history for Gate G1, in the import_history.py record format. No U1, U2 or I2 precedents by design (SPEC §13).

records.what_happened: ISO 9001 certificate expired 6 days before the request; vendor V-017 has 2 years of on-time delivery.
records.why: the vendor check blocks the vendor outright, but the vendor was otherwise in good standing and renewal was in progress.
records.outcome: renewed certificate received in 3 days; PO released.
records.lesson: a recently expired certificate is a hold, not a rejection, when the vendor is otherwise in good standing.

records.what_happened: ISO/IEC 17025 calibration certificate expired 3 days before the request; the renewal audit was already booked; no quality incidents.
records.why: blocking the vendor would have cut off the only nearby calibrated gauge supplier for an administrative lapse.
records.outcome: renewed certificate received in 5 days; PO released.
records.lesson: a recently expired certificate is a hold, not a rejection, when the vendor is otherwise in good standing.

records.what_happened: line 2 stopped on a failed spindle; cost centre CC-MACH was 5% over its annual budget after this order.
records.why: the budget check blocks the order, but the line was down and the overrun was small (5%).
records.outcome: line restarted the next day; controller approved the overrun.
records.lesson: an emergency overrun of up to 10% with the line down is allowed with line-down evidence and controller sign-off.

records.what_happened: line 4 down on a hydraulic leak; the order took CC-MACH 8% over budget.
records.why: waiting for next quarter's budget would have kept line 4 down; the overrun was under 10%.
records.outcome: seals fitted in 2 days; controller signed off.
records.lesson: an emergency overrun of up to 10% with the line down is allowed with line-down evidence and controller sign-off.

records.what_happened: approver E-107 was on leave for 8 days; delegate E-115 holds a valid delegation up to ₹2,00,000.
records.why: the approver was on leave and the request would otherwise wait eight days.
records.outcome: delegate E-115 approved the same day.
records.lesson: when the approver is away and the amount is within the delegate's limit, route to the delegate.

records.what_happened: approver on leave for a week; a valid delegation up to ₹2,00,000 was on file.
records.why: the approver was away and the service slot would have been lost.
records.outcome: delegate approved; service done on schedule.
records.lesson: when the approver is away and the amount is within the delegate's limit, route to the delegate.

records.what_happened: the approver was on leave; the delegation was valid; the request was capex, after the 1 Jul 2026 policy memo.
records.why: the approver was away; under the 1 Jul 2026 memo a capex delegate approval needs Finance Controller co-sign.
records.lesson: since 1 Jul 2026, capex approved by a delegate also needs the Finance Controller's co-sign.

records.what_happened: a request 3% off an earlier one to the same vendor two weeks before; it was the second shipment of the same order, split by the vendor.
records.why: the duplicate check flags a split shipment as a duplicate order.
records.outcome: linked to the master PO; no double payment.
records.lesson: a split shipment of one order is linked to its master PO, not rejected as a duplicate, when the vendor has no duplicate-invoice history.

records.what_happened: a request 2% off an earlier one to the same vendor in the same month; the vendor split the delivery.
records.why: the duplicate check can't tell a split delivery from a repeat order.
records.outcome: linked to the master PO; balance delivered.
records.lesson: a split shipment of one order is linked to its master PO, not rejected as a duplicate, when the vendor has no duplicate-invoice history.

records.what_happened: vendor V-031 changed its bank account 9 days before the request, by email.
records.why: the bank check only flags the change; it says nothing about whether the change is genuine, and a changed account is a classic payment-fraud route.
records.outcome: callback to the number on file confirmed the new account; PO released after 2 days.
records.lesson: a recent bank change means a callback on a known number and a payment hold before anything else.

records.what_happened: the vendor emailed new bank details 5 days before the request.
records.why: a bank change by email can't be trusted until it is confirmed through a known number.
records.lesson: a recent bank change means a callback on a known number and a payment hold before anything else.

records.what_happened: only one quote, because the vendor is the only approved source for this grade.
records.why: three quotes are impossible for a sole-source item.
records.outcome: sole-source form filed; category head signed; PO issued.
records.lesson: a sole-source item above ₹2,00,000 needs the sole-source form and category head sign-off instead of three quotes.

records.what_happened: one quote; the customer drawing names this vendor.
records.why: the customer's specification leaves a single source.
records.outcome: form filed and signed; PO issued.
records.lesson: a sole-source item above ₹2,00,000 needs the sole-source form and category head sign-off instead of three quotes.

records.what_happened: line 1 down; CC-MACH 6% over budget; approver E-104 on leave with delegate E-112 up to ₹2,00,000.
records.why: delegates don't approve budget overruns, even within their limit, so routing to the delegate would have stalled.
records.removed: ROUTE_DELEGATE, because a delegate may not approve an overrun; routed to the next-level approver instead.
records.outcome: plant head approved within hours; line restarted next day.
records.lesson: when the approver is away and the budget overruns, route to the next-level approver, not the delegate.

records.what_happened: line 3 stopped; V-031 changed bank details 12 days earlier; CC-MACH 7% over budget.
records.why: the plain combination holds the PO until the bank callback, which would have kept line 3 down; a PO is not a payment.
records.removed: HOLD_PO, because the PO was released while payment stayed held until the callback.
records.outcome: parts arrived next day; callback confirmed the account; payment released after controller sign-off.
records.lesson: when a bank change meets a line-down overrun, release the PO but hold the payment until the callback.

records.text: Policy memo effective 1 Jul 2026: for capex requests, when the approver is on leave, the delegate may approve only with Finance Controller co-sign (ADD_CONTROLLER_SIGNOFF).
